accessibility:
- **A named landmark:** it's a `<nav>`, named by its visible title through `aria-labelledby`, so a
  screen reader's list of landmarks tells it apart from the site's main navigation. Change the name
  with `labels.title`.
- **Real links:** each entry is an `<a href="#id">`, so it works before hydration, opens in a new
  tab, and can be shared. Following one is the browser's own jump, so the next Tab moves on from the
  section the reader picked, where a scripted scroll would send it back to the list.
- **One current link:** the current link alone has `aria-current="location"`, ARIA's token for where
  you are within a page, never `page`, since the page hasn't changed, and never on more than one
  link.
- **Lists stay lists:** each `MenuList` restates `role="list"`, which Bulma's list reset strips in
  Safari.
- **Not hidden under a sticky header:** with `scroll-padding-top` on the page, a jump lands below
  the header, as WCAG's Focus Not Obscured asks. With `isSticky`, the list keeps room around its
  links for a focus ring, which its scrolling would clip otherwise.
- **No motion of its own:** smooth scrolling is your page's CSS, inside
  `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, and the list scrolls itself instantly.
- **Forced colors:** the current link keeps Menu's bar in the system's Highlight color, since forced
  colors replaces Bulma's fill.
summary: The `TableOfContents` component lists a long page's sections as links in Bulma's menu look, and marks the one being read. It's a `<nav>` named by its title, holding `MenuList` and `MenuItem` links to each `#id`, rendered in full on the server. `useScrollSpy` picks the current section, and its link alone gets `is-active` and `aria-current="location"`. Use the hook on its own to mark the section in view somewhere else, such as an app's nav `Menu`.

props.name: items
props.type: { id: string; label: React.ReactNode; children?: TableOfContentsItem[] }[]
props.description: **Required.** The sections, in page order, as links to their ids. Each link is a plain `<a href="#id">`, so following one is the browser's own jump: put `scroll-padding-top` on the page to land clear of a sticky header, and smooth scrolling, if you want it, in page CSS inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`.

props.name: onActiveChange
props.description: Called with the current section's id when it changes, or `null` above the first section. Never called on the server or before hydration.

props.name: offset
props.description: Pixels from the viewport's top where a section counts as reached. Unset, it's the page's `scroll-padding-top`, so the highlight agrees with where a jump lands under a sticky header.

props.name: isSticky
props.description: Sticks to the top of the viewport as the page scrolls, at `--bulma-table-of-contents-sticky-top`, and scrolls itself when it's taller than the viewport. Adds `is-sticky`.
